title: Google, Constellation near $1 billion-plus nuclear power deal, Bloomberg reports
source_used: Bloomberg text as carried by The Edge Malaysia; Investing.com summary on Yahoo Finance UK (the pool link)
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on 6 Oct 2026 that Google parent Alphabet is nearing an agreement to buy nuclear energy from Constellation Energy, which Bloomberg calls the biggest US reactor operator.
Google would pay Constellation $1 billion or more over a multi-year agreement that could be announced as soon as this week, according to unnamed people familiar with the discussions.
The exact scale and location of the nuclear capacity could not be determined; Constellation and Google declined to comment on Monday.
Amazon struck a similar deal with Constellation last week: 690 megawatts, including capacity from an upgrade of the Calvert Cliffs plant in Maryland.

Google already has nuclear agreements: with NextEra Energy (backing the restart of the Duane Arnold reactor in Iowa, shut since 2020) and, last month, with Southern Co (funding upgrades at two plants).
Recent tech-company deals have focused on existing nuclear plants because new reactors can take a decade or more to permit and build.
Microsoft agreed in 2024 to buy power from the shuttered Three Mile Island plant, which Constellation plans to restart next year.
quote_evidence: The tech giant is nearing a deal to pay Constellation US$1 billion or more over the course of a multi-year agreement that’s expected to be announced as soon as this week, according to people familiar with the discussions, who asked not to be named because the information is private.
The exact scale and location of the nuclear capacity couldn’t be determined.
Amazon.com Inc struck a similar deal last week with Constellation.
why_it_matters_hint: Tech companies are locking in round-the-clock nuclear power for AI data centers; this deal, if it is confirmed, would follow Amazon's similar deal with Constellation last week.
event_date: Reported 6 Oct 2026 by Bloomberg; the deal itself is not yet announced.
notes: Bloomberg is the first reporter. Read Bloomberg's full text as carried by The Edge Malaysia (theedgemalaysia.com/node/820651) and the Investing.com summary on Yahoo Finance UK. Single report from unnamed sources; no confirmation from Google or Constellation. The Bloomberg page itself was not opened (paywalled).
